moving_parts.quote: The OptiCool from Quantum Design is equipped with a powerful PT cryo-cooler, as it not only has to generate liquid helium for temperature control up to 1.7 K, but also cools the superconducting 7 T magnet.
a unique, single-cooler design that provides cooling for both the magnet and the circulating helium
The bipolar design also allows smooth continuous ramping through zero field.

notes: Standard OptiCool 7 T with X300 (16 wires = 8 twisted pairs) and X310 (4 coax to 20 GHz). Geometry: cryostat block on optical table (1 m x 0.5 m x 1 m min), split-coil conical magnet with magnet axis vertical, sample pod inserted from the top into the Temperature Control Column; 7 side windows (40 mm, 24.5 mm clear bore, 13 deg full angle) around the horizontal plane and 1 top window (50 mm, 41.5 mm clear bore, 70 deg full angle at magnet centre). Optional bottom window (X240) not included. Vibration <10 nm horizontal / <4 nm vertical peak-to-peak. Field uniformity 0.3% over a 3 cm DSV. Cooler type (pulse tube) comes from a QD Europe news article, not the QD USA spec sheet, which only says 'single-cooler design'.
